title: Microhandoff Blitz — short-form announce & Q&A
body:
Purpose:
Quick internal announcement and short Q&A script for tomorrow’s accelerated handoff window (2-4 hour blitz) while we perform capacity rebalancing. This is a user-facing-lite internal comms piece: short, empathetic, and action-focused for SRE, support, and oncall engineers.

TL;DR (one-liners to use):
- Heads-up: We will briefly shift traffic and throttle burst capacity tomorrow 04:00-06:00 PT to complete a rolling capacity rebalance. Impact: brief latency bump for low-priority background workloads; customer-facing APIs on premium tier unaffected by design.
- If you see elevated 5xx or latency on hosted-api, escalate to #ops-bridge and tag @oncall. Use INF-1972 for tracing.

Audience: SRE, platform oncall, support L2, solutions engineering standby.

When to post (channels):
- 03:30 PT: Internal pre-alert in #ops-bridge and #platform-status (one-liner).
- 04:00 PT: Short status pin in #platform-status noting start.
- 04:30 PT: Midpoint check-in if any customer-facing anomaly observed.
- 06:00 PT: Close-out note with brief summary + follow-ups.

Suggested short announcement text (copy/paste friendly):
"Planned short window 04:00–06:00 PT: backend capacity rebalance. Expect transient latency on low-priority batch workloads; premium customer endpoints should remain within SLOs. Ops team monitoring. If you observe customer-facing errors, notify #ops-bridge and reference JIRA INF-1972."

All-hands talking points (for anyone dropping into team syncs):
- Why: rebalance to reduce tail latency for region eu-west and free up capacity for Dedicated pilot.
- Impact: intentionally risk-limited — only background pipelines and non-critical batching throttled.
- Mitigation: automated fallback to smaller model variant + circuit breakers enabled.
- Post-mortem: quick retro if any customer impact.

Anticipated questions + scripted answers (short):
Q: Will customer-facing latency increase?
A: Not expected for premium routes — we routed traffic away from affected pools. If you spot anything, raise immediately in #ops-bridge.

Q: Why not perform this at 02:00 PT?
A: We aligned with our usage heatmap. 04:00 PT gives slightly lower background pressure for EU workloads without disrupting regional teams.

Q: Will Dedicated customers see impact?
A: No. Dedicated capacity pools are isolated. Notify account manager if you get direct customer notes.

Escalation steps (short):
1) If customer-facing 5xx or latency > SLO for > 5 minutes, post in #ops-bridge and ping @oncall.
2) Add a short comment to JIRA INF-1972 with timestamp and service hit.
3) If degradation persists > 20 minutes, open incident bridge and pull product support.

Checklist for comm owners (tick before 03:30 PT):
- [ ] Post pre-alert in #ops-bridge (03:30 PT).
- [ ] Add calendar note for ops on-call.
- [ ] Confirm rollback knobs are ready and tested: model-variant fallback, autoscaler override, prefix-cache flush.
- [ ] Notify Sales/CS L2 for any high-touch customers scheduled in the window.

Notes-to-self / unresolved items (quick):
- Confirm whether EU telemetry filter will drop debug traces during rebalance (ask telemetry team @Lina).
- Check whether Optimize recommendations triggered an autoscaler bump last night (possible race with this window).
- Decide whether to stitch a short postmortem template into the close-out note (lean toward yes).

Post-window close-out template (one-liner):
"Window closed at 06:00 PT. Rebalance completed; no customer-facing impact observed / OR <brief impact summary>. Follow-ups: <owner> to file postmortem by EOD tomorrow."

Personal reminders (for Marcel):
- Bring this note to 03:20 ops huddle.
- Ask Meera to confirm that the Dedicated pools are not in auto-burst.
- Draft 2-sentence external note if CS asks (keep to facts + apology + next steps).

Unresolved decisions to capture after window:
- Decide on retaining the temporary throttle for 48h vs immediate rollback.
- Confirm telemetry retention for rebalance traces (for later analysis).

End of note. Keep this short in comms — we do not need long explanations in Slack, lean into quick facts and calls to action.

-- Marcel
